title: Predicted enzyme structures support shared substrate gates in C-glycosylation
summary: Analysis of structural models for 56 C-active UGT enzymes found acceptor gates throughout the set and two enzymes lacking a discernible donor gate; AlphaFold3 and source-labeled RobettaFold models supported variable open/closed gate conformations. These predictions extended a gating hypothesis derived from experimental structures and molecular simulations, rather than independently measuring dynamics across all enzymes. For maize ZmUGT708A6, crystallography, biochemical/mutational tests and QM/MM calculations supported a stepwise C-glycosylation mechanism involving water-mediated stabilization of a high-energy sigma complex. The AI contribution concerns comparison of predicted gate architectures; direct mechanistic tests focused on selected enzymes and substrates.
organization: Freie Universität Berlin; Technical University of Denmark

evidence.tested: The predicted gate conformations were compared across 56 UGT models; mechanistic propositions were tested with crystallography, biochemical assays, mutational data, QM/MM and pH/substrate activity experiments.
evidence.unknown: Predicted conformations across the 56 enzymes are not direct measurements of their dynamics. Supplementary model-generation details were not assessed here; the reviewed experimental/mechanistic scope centers on selected enzymes and substrates.
evidence.ai_role: AlphaFold3 and source-labeled RobettaFold structural models were compared to assess gate architecture/conformational variability across 56 C-active UGTs; experimental structures and simulations established the core gating/mechanistic hypothesis.

source_review.scope: Publisher article abstract; selected gate-architecture and reaction-mechanism Results; computational/crystallographic Methods; contributions and affiliations. Supplementary model-generation material was not reviewed.
